newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power prices steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power prices steady to higher.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West were mostly steady to higher Tuesday with some strength in the northern areas due to cold weather demand, brokers and marketers said.
Temperatures in North Dakota and Minnesota were forecast to reach highs in the 20s and 30s degrees Fahrenheit on Wednesday, maintaining significant electrical demand, the sources said.
"It's still cold, and when marketers are doing business they are having to buy from utilities which are reluctant to part with their power due to the demand," one Mid-West marketer said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Wednesday delivery were pegged steady at $25.00-27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Wednesday delivery was pegged higher at $23.00-25.00 from $21.00-25.00 on Monday, the sources said.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Wednesday delivery were assessed at $21.00-24.00 from $19.00-22.00 on Monday, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
January and February peak ECAR prices were pegged at $23.40-23.80 per MWh.

In the Southwest Power Pool (SPP), peak non-firm power prices for Wednesday delivery were talked steady at $20.00-22.00 although some price discussion was said to be held at higher levels early in the day.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged higher at $26.75-27.25 from $25.75-26.25 per MWh on Monday, the sources said.
